newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria investigates NNPC foreign accounts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria investigates NNPC foreign accounts - paper.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has sent abroad a fact-finding team to investigate claims made by officials of state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) and Central Bank on balances left in their foreign accounts, the head of a government agency said.

Sam Aluko, chairman of the National Economic Intelligence Committee (NEIC), said the team will determine the true position of the deposits left in the foreign accounts. He did not name members of the team.
"The NNPC and Central Bank people lied to (Head of State) General Sani Abacha that they had little or nothing in their accounts abroad," said Aluko, quoted by Thisday newspaper on Sunday.

"I told the Head of State they lied; I told him that they have 43 accounts in the United Kingdom," adding: "I'm aware of the existence of a secret account where the corporation has a deposit of $53 million."
NNPC and banking sector regulator Central Bank had been plagued with mismanagement and fraud resulting in the sacking of staff from both firms early in the year.
In June, 3,000 NNPC workers were laid-off based on the recommendation of a panel on reorganisation of the corporation to enhance efficiency.
A month earlier, almost 700 Central Bank staff were given the boot for various offences ranging from fraud and indiscipline to lack of productivity.
NNPC is in joint-ventures with foreign oil companies to pump almost two million barrels of crude oil per day which accounts for more than 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings.

It manages Nigeria's four refineries which in theory can produce 445,000 bpd but has been reduced to much less due to mismanagement and a lack of finance to buy needed spare parts to carry out repairs.
